# A native titlebar drop into the MAIN window never parks: the focus gate needs a user activation the OS drag cannot grant

## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-09-02 on the Workstation: pop a pane out, drag the popup by its OS titlebar over the main window — the drop-zone highlight follows correctly — release: nothing happens. The popup stays, the pane never comes home. Popup-over-popup drops (PR #18059's path) work.

Read live through the Neural Link on the operator's Workstation minutes after the attempt (main session `31120d5a…`, the app's own receipts):

- `DragCoordinator.claimTrace`: every entry `outcome: claimed, claimedStableId: workstation-main`, the main window `intersects: true, accepts: true`, the popup skipped as source. The hover half works; each gesture produced a valid candidate.
- `Workspace.lastVesselParkReceipt`: `authority.source*` all `true`, `targetHasHandle: false` / `targetFocusCapable: false` (informational — the main window has no opener-minted route and the check is exempted for a main target), `focused: false`, `refusedAt: 'focus'`, no `moved` key. The park returned at the focus step before ever moving the popup.
- `lastCrossWindowTransfer: null`, `tearOutPanes: {}` after the popup was closed by hand.
- No console errors or warnings in either realm; `nativeGestures: []` afterwards — the gesture ended by itself.

This is the same receipt #18054 read on 2026-09-01. PR #18055 made the refused park a bounded retry (`nativeWindowDispositionRetryMs` 250 ms doubling, capped at 5 s, `nativeWindowParkRetryLimit` 6 → about 12.75 s in total) on the premise that focus "starts succeeding the moment the window server lets go". For a main-window target it does not.

## The Problem

The native-titlebar terminal is geometry-only by design: no pointer event reaches the page while the OS drags a window, so `onWindowPositionChange` arms a candidate over a claimed target and commits after dwell (450 ms on the same target) + settle (250 ms without a geometry update). `commitNativeWindowDrop` then asks the source zone to **park** the popup strictly — `parkTearOutVessel({nativeTitlebar: true})` (`apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs`) — and the park's first step is to give the TARGET window focus, so the parked popup falls behind it in z-order.

For a popup target the focus verb is `Neo.Main.windowNativeFocus` on the opener's handle — the opener focusing a window it opened, which the platform permits. For a **main** target the root window has no route, so the verb is `Neo.Main.windowFocus({windowId: popup})`: the popup's main thread calls `window.opener.focus()`, under the comment "a popup may focus its opener under the user activation carried by the titlebar gesture" (from the original reintegration, PR #16140). An OS titlebar drag delivers **no DOM event** to the popup's document — that is the whole reason this path is geometry-driven — so the popup carries no transient user activation, and Chrome declines a cross-window `focus()` without one. `#focusWindow` (`src/Main.mjs`) verifies by polling the target document's `hasFocus()` six times at 50 ms and truthfully answers `false`. Releasing the titlebar changes nothing: the popup keeps focus after an OS drag, still without activation. Every retry gets the same `false`; after the seventh attempt `retryNativeWindowPark` ends the gesture, the highlight disappears, and the only reintegration a human can reach is closing the popup.

The rigs pass because headless Chromium lets every window claim focus (`#focusWindow`'s own comment notes it): `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL` moves the popup with CDP and the park's focus succeeds without any activation — the freedom the human path never has.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs` — `onWindowPositionChange` (candidate + dwell/settle), `commitNativeWindowDrop` (phase `parking` → `suspendWindowDrag` → on `suspended !== true` → `retryNativeWindowPark`), `retryNativeWindowPark` (backoff, `nativeWindowParkRetryLimit`), `settleNativeWindowDisposition` (close/restore retries).
- `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs#parkTearOutVessel` — the authority table + receipt; `targetIsMain` selects `Neo.Main.windowFocus` for the focus verb; the chain is focus → `windowNativeMoveTo` to the target frame origin → refocus → `parked: true`. The move and the later close (`retireNativeWindowDrag` → `windowNativeClose`) run from the MAIN realm through the popup's owner-granted handle, which needs no activation — the popup-over-popup path proves both work.
- `src/Main.mjs#windowFocus` — documented for the keyboard-command return path ("the popup holds the keystroke's user activation"); the titlebar path reuses it without the activation the doc names.
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/DragTarget.mjs` — hooks `suspendWindowDrag` / `onRemoteDrop` / `onRemoteDropOut`; a `suspendWindowDrag` answer of `true` is the strict park, `false` a refusal (retry), anything else non-strict.

## The Fix

The focus gate exists so the parked popup sits behind the target during the embodiment handoff. For a main target on the native path that goal has another route: the source is retired (closed) right after the semantic commit anyway, and macOS/Windows return focus to the app's remaining window when the focused popup closes. So:

1. `parkTearOutVessel`: when `targetIsMain && nativeTitlebar`, the focus step and the refocus step become **best-effort** — attempt them, record `focused` / `refocused` truthfully in the receipt, but do not return `false` on their refusal and do not compensate the move on a refused refocus. The **move** (`windowNativeMoveTo` to the target frame origin, from the main realm through the handle) stays the strict gate: it is refused while the OS still drags the window and succeeds the moment the user lets go — the release detector #18054 wanted, on a verb the platform actually grants without activation.
2. The receipt gains `parkAttempts` and keeps the last `refusedAt`, so a stalled retry is readable live (the step #18055 named and did not land).
3. No change to the popup-target branch (`windowNativeFocus` on the owner's handle keeps working) or to the coordinator's retry shape.
4. Witness: a unit arm on `parkTearOutVessel` with a stubbed `Neo.Main` whose `windowFocus` answers `false` and whose `windowNativeMoveTo` answers `false` then `true` (the OS hold, then the release) — red on `dev` (returns `false` at focus, never moves), green at head (moves on the second attempt, `parked: true`, receipt shows `focused: false`); a control arm for a popup target where a refused `windowNativeFocus` still refuses the park. The existing NL specs stay green (they grant focus). The human check stays a Post-Merge item with the operator as owner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A native titlebar drop onto the main window commits once the user releases: the popup parks (moves behind the main frame origin), the proxy embodies, `transferItem` applies, the popup retires — with no click into the main window required.
- [ ] AC-2 `parkTearOutVessel` on a main target under `nativeTitlebar` treats focus/refocus as best-effort and the move as the strict gate; the receipt records `focused`, `refocused`, `parkAttempts`, `refusedAt` truthfully. Red-first unit arm on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-3 A popup target still refuses the park when `windowNativeFocus` is refused (control arm).
- [ ] AC-4 `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL` and `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL` green under the Brain root; `unit/manager` green.
- [ ] AC-5 Operator hand check on the Workstation: drag a popup over main by its titlebar, release, no further input — the pane comes home within the retry window. Post-Merge item, operator-owned.

## Out of Scope

- The keyboard-command focus return path (`windowFocus` under a keystroke's activation) — unchanged.
- Pointer-path cross-window drags (#17578).
- Detecting the OS release by any other signal; the move's success remains the detector.
- The spring-loaded dwell interaction the operator chose on 2026-09-02 (the drop area fills over the dwell, the transfer commits on completion, the popup closes after — no park at all for main targets): its own ticket, layered on top of this fix.

## Avoided Traps

- **Reading a green rig as proof of the human path.** `#focusWindow` documents that headless platforms let every window claim focus; the two NL specs pass for exactly that reason. The witness for this ticket stubs the refusal instead of trusting the platform, and the human check stays owned.
- **Widening the retry window.** More retries of a verb the platform never grants only delay the silent end; the fix moves the gate to a verb that IS granted on release.
- **Skipping the move gate too.** Parking while the OS still holds the window is what #18054 measured as the first failure mode; the move must stay strict so the popup is parked only once it is free.
